DESCRIPTION: FIND — `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceStore.verify_bundle()`. The method iterates with `zip(bundle.records, bundle.inclusion_proofs)`. If the bundle is malformed with unequal list lengths, extra records or extra proofs are silently ignored and the method can return success for an incomplete verification. Evidence: Python `zip()` truncates to the shorter input; there is no explicit length equality check before `return len(errors) == 0, errors`.
FOLLOW: This breaks bundle-verification completeness. A tampered bundle can drop the proof for the last record, or add unattested records after the verified prefix, and `verify_bundle()` still reports success as long as the paired prefix verifies. Because bundle export/verification is a headline feature of this module, this yields a silently wrong audit result rather than a mere edge case.

DESCRIPTION: FIND — `bench/evidence.py`, `_classify_event()`. For `artifact_type == "verdict"` it returns the literal `"verdict"` for every finding reference instead of mapping the verdict action to one of the required semantic classes CONFIRM/CHALLENGE/EXTEND/MERGE. Evidence: the function has explicit parsing logic only under `atype == "model_chat_log"` and then a generic `if atype == "verdict": return "verdict"`. The task contract for this module explicitly says event classification should correctly identify CONFIRM/CHALLENGE/EXTEND/MERGE. Verdict records referencing a finding will never be classified into those buckets.
FOLLOW: Provenance traces become incomplete at the semantic level: a finding can have an actual verdict artifact in the chain, but `trace_finding()` emits a generic `"verdict"` event and `_describe_event()` falls through to “referenced in verdict record”. Any consumer counting confirmations/challenges/extensions/merges from traces will undercount or mislabel these events. This is silently wrong output, not cosmetic.
